verdicts.strongest_argument: Two things hold this at the midpoint. First, the item codes say it was announced: an 8-K carrying item 5.02 with item 9.01 means an exhibit was furnished, which for a management change is a press release, so the company put it on a wire. Victoria's Secret is a $7.1bn consumer name that trades 1.5m shares a day and is covered by every retail-sector desk; a management change there is reported the same morning. The reason it is absent from this corpus is that no news search was run for this ticker and the stored stream is retail brand banter - a capture artefact, not evidence the market missed it. Second, the chronology in the finding does not hold. It says the 8-K sits 'inside the window in which the stock fell from $102 to $83 in seven business days', but the corpus quote recording that fall is dated 2026-08-18T18:42:03Z, two days BEFORE the 2026-08-20 filing - so the 19% drawdown was already complete when the 8-K was filed and cannot have been caused by it, nor can the 8-K be the unexplained cause the finding is looking for. What is left is an unread item code with no direction: 5.02 covers appointments and compensatory arrangements as readily as departures, no body is stored, and the stated lean ('departures get filed before results') is an unsourced base-rate assertion. The 13D/A of 07-29 adds an unnamed holder with an unstated stake.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The hunter concedes the components are 'individually all wire copy' and the capture confirms every one of them. UBS's raise to $95 from $90 on 2026-08-18, the second house's $80 mark, and the short-interest and squeeze discussion are all in the stored body at entries dated 2026-08-18T16:31:02Z, 2026-08-25T12:23:08Z and 2026-08-26T15:57:38Z (docs/621d0cd2f2ce628fcfa8161af1d684a409ae43e9.txt, admissible snapshots). The remaining two facts - the stock is 269% above its 52-week low and the prior print produced +47.44% - are fields in the sealed baseline, which is to say the market's own record of what it has already done. Combining published targets with a published price to observe that the stock trades above the sell-side's marks is subtraction on public numbers, and it is a permanent condition of any stock that has tripled: targets lag price by construction, in every squeeze, always. That is structural, not novel. The mechanism is also self-cancelling in the way the finding admits: 'a print that merely meets expectations removes the squeeze fuel' and 'a genuine short base can be squeezed further' are the two halves of a coin, and nothing in the capture gives a short-interest figure from an exchange source to weight them.
